video_title: TomorrowX: Brian Armstrong, Gavin Baker, Andrew Feldman & More
gist: A string of short TomorrowX (Austin) interviews: Gavin Baker argues the market's AI-ROI math ignores open-source and enterprise demand (Fireworks, Dell AI factories) and lobbies for Jensen Huang's return amid an Nvidia CEO crisis and China chip-policy fight; Cerebras, Zipline (Uber Eats, Walmart), Coinbase, Vercel, Saronic and Eight Sleep leaders cover fast inference, autonomous logistics at scale, agentic finance, an AI-driven wave of hacks, US shipbuilding gaps and human-enhancement drugs.

insights.claim: Gavin Baker argues the market's AI ROI math is flawed: it compares ~$1-2 trillion of capex against only ~$120B of Anthropic (~$80B) plus OpenAI (~$40B) revenue and under $200B total, ignoring open-source and enterprise on-prem AI demand.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: AI-capex bears may be undercounting returns; open-source and enterprise AI demand is invisible in headline lab revenue.
insights.quote: all we have to show for it is 80 billion in anthropic revenue. Um, plus the open AI revenue and you know, it seems like that's been reported to be around 40.

insights.claim: Fireworks (serving and customizing open-source models) has seen its top customer grow 13x in the first nine to ten months of the year, per Gavin Baker relaying Fireworks executive Lynn Chow; Fireworks is an Atreides portfolio company.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Open-source inference providers are a fast-growing, under-tracked demand pool.
insights.quote: their top customer. is 13xed in the first uh nine or 10 months of this year

insights.claim: Because margins on open-source tokens are lower, the open-source ecosystem drags proportionally more compute demand with it than closed-model revenue suggests.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Compute demand per dollar of AI revenue is higher in open-source, supporting semis demand.
insights.quote: because the margins are lower on these open source tokens, it drags more compute demand with it

insights.claim: Dell sold 3,200 'AI factories' to enterprises in 2024-25 and about 3,300 in the last nine months alone, meaning 6,000+ enterprises run open-source AI on Dell GPU servers, demand absent from the market's ROI calculation.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Enterprise on-prem AI adoption is accelerating; bullish for Dell and GPU suppliers.
insights.quote: in the first two years of offering AI factories, which is 24 and 25, they sold 3,200 of them. And they've sold, I believe, 3,300 in the last 9 months.

insights.claim: Gavin Baker reports conference commentary showed AI demand strong and accelerating (Cerebras, SpaceX compute demand, a CEO whose business accelerated since earnings two weeks prior), while stocks trade as if there is an imminent demand problem.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Disconnect between ground-level fundamentals and AI stock prices could be an entry point.
insights.quote: stocks are trading like there is an imminent issue with demand and I just don't think that's what we've heard here today

insights.claim: Baker frames the market as in a Buffett 'voting machine' phase fixated on second derivatives (peak growth rate); if AI is like a 60-year railroad build-out, Nvidia and most AI stocks are cheap even at 5-10% annual growth beyond next year's guide, with 2027 guidance as the weighing catalyst.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Watch 2027 guides; the 'growth peaked = it's over' heuristic may be wrong for long-cycle infrastructure.
insights.quote: let's say they grow 8% a year 5% a year 10% a year it's a cheap stock it's a cheap stock

insights.claim: Andrew Feldman says the market has swung toward valuing inference speed: a year and a half ago customers questioned why speed mattered, now daily users demand it, and Cerebras claims 10-15x faster AI compute than alternatives with demand 'off the chart'.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: Fast inference is becoming a purchasing criterion, favoring specialized inference silicon.
insights.quote: we build the fastest AI compute on Earth. Not by a little bit, but 10 or 15x.

insights.claim: Cerebras, which already counts OpenAI as a customer, won AWS, Microsoft and Oracle as customers in the last six months, following its IPO this year.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler adoption validates Cerebras' fast-inference positioning.
insights.quote: we we we have OpenAI as a customer but in the last 6 months we we won AWS and Microsoft and and Oracle pretty good six months.

insights.claim: Feldman views the recent cyber/airline chaos as a once-in-30-years confluence of unlucky events rather than a new normal, and expects AI demand to keep 'ripping', models to improve, and open-source models to keep closing in with the open vs closed battle intensifying.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: CEO-level read that recent selloff drivers are transient.
insights.quote: I don't think people should think of of the tough last week as sort of the the new normal.

insights.claim: Feldman argues a working system is weakest during an upgrade (e.g., the air traffic control failure during a copper-to-fiber or router change), and that data center failures like a recent Microsoft outage are rare once-in-a-decade events.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: Migration periods are the risk window for infrastructure operators.
insights.quote: a working system uh is at its weakest when you try and change it.

insights.claim: Feldman argues data centers create high-paying multi-year construction jobs (hence labor-union support in many states) and, via cloud and AI, enable small-business and creator job creation.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: Counter-narrative to data-center local opposition; relevant to permitting politics.

themes.theme: Nvidia CEO crisis, China and export controls

insights.claim: Gavin Baker and Brad Gerstner sent a letter to the Nvidia board urging a slow, deliberate approach, noting CFO Colette is superb and there is no need to rush, and—if facts clear him—considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Major shareholders are lobbying for Jensen's return; CEO succession is a live Nvidia risk/catalyst.
insights.quote: There is no need to rush to hire another CEO.

insights.claim: Baker warns that Jensen, who is not charged with anything and will testify to Congress amid an independent investigation, could become CEO of a Nvidia competitor if not brought back.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Key-person risk for Nvidia extends to competitive threat.
insights.quote: he could go be the CEO of a competitor

insights.claim: Baker argues new US chip policies replacing Jensen's approach force China to build its own ecosystem: with Huawei hardware now used by every Chinese AI lab, it could improve quickly, posing grave national-security risk.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Tighter restrictions may accelerate a rival Chinese AI hardware stack (bearish long-term for Nvidia's China moat).
insights.quote: Now that Huawei hardware is going to be used by every Chinese AI lab. Like it might get better really fast.

insights.claim: Baker says Jensen's relationships with the Asian supply chain are unparalleled—no contract with TSMC, reportedly once offered the TSMC CEO role by Morris Chang—letting him secure more volume at lower prices; Taiwan has lit up buildings with 'Bring Jensen back' signs.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Loss of Jensen could weaken Nvidia's supply-chain allocation advantage.
insights.quote: He's never had a contract with Taiwan Semi.

insights.claim: A poker champion and game theorist (Just Games founder) calls the 'lock China into the US tech stack' argument for selling advanced chips convoluted: China won't be locked in, is ahead on energy and chip-bottlenecked, so extra chips help it at the margin.
insights.speaker: Poker champion / Just Games founder
insights.so_what: Argues for stricter export controls; contrary view to Nvidia-friendly policy.
insights.quote: China already has like is performing better than we do on energy. They are bottlenecked by chips.

insights.claim: The Just Games founder cites Anthropic reportedly switching to AMD chips in 3 days versus 6-12 months previously, arguing software-based hardware moats erode as models improve—Jensen's 'I'm not a car' becomes 'now you're a car'.
insights.speaker: Poker champion / Just Games founder
insights.so_what: Falling switching costs threaten CUDA-style lock-in and Nvidia's pricing power.
insights.quote: anthropic reported that they were able to switch to AMD chips from one tax to another where it took them 6 to 12 months before to only 3 days

insights.claim: He notes the latest Chinese models were trained at least partly on Blackwells, and that China is refusing H20s to push Huawei chips to DeepSeek, behaving as an ideological rather than capitalist actor.
insights.speaker: Poker champion / Just Games founder
insights.so_what: Chip leakage to China and Chinese self-sufficiency push are ongoing policy risks.
insights.quote: We've seen that uh the last Chinese models were all trained at least in part uh on black wells

insights.claim: The Just Games founder warns that executives' shareholder-value-motivated arguments (e.g., on China chip sales) are being treated as disinterested policy philosophy, breaking public sense-making.
insights.speaker: Poker champion / Just Games founder
insights.so_what: Discount incentive-driven policy advocacy.

insights.claim: The Vercel CEO suggests some parties building fully proprietary ecosystems benefit from Nvidia's fall because Nvidia funded open-weight alternatives (e.g., Nemotron), alongside shorts and geopolitics—'study the matrix' of motives.
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Nvidia's turmoil may have competitive/strategic beneficiaries.
insights.quote: if you're building a fully proprietary ecosystem and and Nvidia is trying to like fund the openweight alternative

insights.claim: The Vercel CEO points to Chinese dominance in video models (Seedance) and TikTok's data scale as a cautionary tale for letting China build first-party everything rather than depend on the US.
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Data scale is a durable advantage in generative video.

themes.theme: Open vs. closed AI and agentic finance

insights.claim: Brian Armstrong says Coinbase is building AI-enabled financial accounts and payment rails so agents can form teams, hire each other and pay in real time globally, as part of decentralizing AI via a marketplace of open-weight models.
insights.speaker: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase CEO)
insights.so_what: Agent payments are a new product vector for crypto rails.
insights.quote: an AI enabled financial account the payment rails so that agents can assemble into teams, hire each other, make payments in real time all over the world

insights.claim: Gavin Baker wants a vibrant American open-source AI ecosystem because AI systems embed value systems; he sees Jensen as its biggest proponent and fears a world of one to three frontier AIs.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Open-source AI policy is tied to Nvidia leadership and US politics.
insights.quote: I do not want to live in a world dominated by one, two or three frontier AIs because these AI systems are imbued with value systems.

insights.claim: The Just Games founder predicts the gap between closed and open-weight models will likely widen absent more open-ecosystem funding, as labs stop selling tokens and build products; closed models will matter most for scientific and medical breakthroughs.
insights.speaker: Poker champion / Just Games founder
insights.so_what: Frontier labs may shift from API to products, widening the capability gap.
insights.quote: unfortunately likely it's going to grow absent uh some more funding being collected for uh an open ecosystem

insights.claim: Baker estimates from third-party data that SpaceX's first-party AI business (Grokbot) is approaching ~$10B of very high-margin, fast-growing revenue, and says he now spends almost more time in Grokbot than on X.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Under-appreciated AI revenue stream inside SpaceX ahead of its IPO.
insights.quote: I think it's getting pretty close to 10 billion that's a very significant amount of very high margin revenue

insights.claim: iConnections' CEO says his team built the website, dashboards and mobile app for a 5,000-person TomorrowX conference in days using AI (Grokbot agents), compressing an 18-month event build into six to seven months; AI gives workers 3-5x leverage.
insights.speaker: Ron (iConnections CEO)
insights.so_what: Agentic tools are delivering real productivity gains in non-tech operations.
insights.quote: this is just giving you three, four, 5x leverage on whatever your skill set is

insights.claim: Harper Carroll predicts AI agents will sit between users and social feeds, filtering slop (as Andrej Karpathy did with a custom YouTube/Hacker News feed), devaluing engagement-optimized feeds and pushing creators toward valuable content.
insights.speaker: Harper Carroll
insights.so_what: Long-term risk to attention-maximizing ad platforms.
insights.quote: just having an AI in between the content like the feed I think will become less valuable

insights.claim: The Vercel CEO says the reward for hacking has risen because AI tokens are now near-currency fungible with dollars, with black markets for tokens and distillation attacks; targets are companies with token access, including North Korean actors.
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Holders of AI compute/tokens face elevated attack risk; security spend rises.
insights.quote: Tokens are very precious. They're fungeable with US dollars, right?

insights.claim: The Vercel CEO's hottest take: there will be many more high-profile hacks ('everything hackable will be hacked'), with possible CrowdStrike-like outages of critical systems in coming weeks and months, before AI defense leaves systems in a strong position.
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Near-term cyber incidents likely; demand for AI security tooling.
insights.quote: everything hackable will be hacked

insights.claim: He argues decades of human-built tech debt must be rebuilt in memory-safe languages and near-provably-unhackable ways, with adversarial agents (mixing proprietary and open models) auditing every commit; Vercel inserts such an agent in its deploy pipeline and open-sourced a harness called DeepSec.
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Infrastructure rewrite cycle and AI code-audit tooling are investable themes.
insights.quote: We can rebuild them in memory safe programming languages.

insights.claim: A recent Chase-related breach came from a compromised third party embedded on the website front end, not Chase itself, per the Vercel CEO; open models were also used defensively (Hugging Face used them to analyze its attack).
insights.speaker: Vercel CEO (G)
insights.so_what: Supply-chain/third-party scripts are the key web attack vector.
insights.quote: it's not because Chase got hacked. It's the third party that got hacked

insights.claim: Brian Armstrong says Coinbase scans every line of code with cyber-expert models before production, designs systems resilient to any single employee's laptop malware, and keeps 99% of crypto offline—underpinning custody for seven of the largest banks, most crypto ETFs, 140 government agencies and 50 of the top 100 hedge funds.
insights.speaker: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase CEO)
insights.so_what: Flight to quality in cyber turmoil favors trusted custodians like Coinbase.
insights.quote: we store 99% of all the crypto entirely offline, airgapped from the internet

insights.claim: Armstrong recommends avoiding SMS-linked 2FA (SIM takeover risk) in favor of YubiKeys or authenticator apps, and says Coinbase Prime offers multi-signer withdrawals, liveness checks against AI deepfakes, and even in-person verification.
insights.speaker: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase CEO)
insights.so_what: AI deepfakes are changing high-net-worth security practices.
insights.quote: Don't link it to your cell phone number because like sometimes your cell phone number can get taken over.

insights.claim: Zipline announced an Uber Eats partnership to reach a million deliveries a day—about a quarter of Uber Eats' US deliveries—across almost every US metro and 1.2 million merchants.
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Autonomous drone delivery is moving to national scale with major platforms.
insights.quote: a million deliveries a day, which is about a quarter of their overall deliveries in the US

insights.claim: Zipline is expanding from 22 to 300 Walmart Supercenters in a first phase, offering 90,000 of ~100,000 SKUs delivered in minutes; average delivery once food is ready is 2-5 minutes.
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Retail last-mile automation scaling; competitive pressure on human courier models.
insights.quote: We're now expanding to 300 Walmart super centers in the first phase.

insights.claim: Zipline has three-plus strategic partners each seeking over a million deliveries a day, turning its whole plan into a 'unit of sale'; it is growing 10-15% week over week and aiming to scale 3-5x faster, with ~25 charging sites in Dallas.
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Demand outstrips supply; the bottleneck is hardware supply-chain scaling.
insights.quote: growing 10 to 15% week over week

insights.claim: Zipline CEO Keller warns investors newly pivoting to hardware underestimate timelines—Tesla took 15 years and SpaceX 20 to reach meaningful scale—and that a project's performance equals its weakest supplier ('a zero anywhere in the chain' makes the whole project zero).
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Expect delays and real-world learning for hardware-heavy VC portfolios over the next 3-4 years.
insights.quote: So if there's a zero anywhere in the chain, then the overall project is a zero.

insights.claim: Keller notes even the best-funded companies, OpenAI and Anthropic, are finding data center builds hard due to regulation, permitting, community acceptance and supply-chain complexity.
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Data center timelines face non-capital bottlenecks.

insights.claim: Keller argues developing nations will choose between a US and Chinese AI/robotics tech stack, and the US should compete there to secure economic and technology leadership.
insights.speaker: Keller (Zipline CEO)
insights.so_what: Global South infrastructure is a geopolitical battleground for US tech exporters.

insights.claim: Gavin Baker says SpaceX's Starship upper-stage catch enables rapid reusability, which unlocks orbital compute (first satellites expected in 2027 per Brad), Starlink direct-to-cell and eventually asteroid mining; SpaceX engineers consider orbital-compute cooling solved.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: Starship reusability is the gating factor for SpaceX's next revenue lines.
insights.quote: Brad earlier today said they're gonna put up the first orbital comput satellites in 2027.

insights.claim: Baker says SpaceX accounts for 85% of mass to orbit, operates 11,000 satellites, and is America's most important national defense contractor; Starlink V3 uses roughly 10-15% the power of an orbital compute satellite.
insights.speaker: Gavin Baker
insights.so_what: SpaceX's launch dominance underpins its strategic and valuation case.
insights.quote: SpaceX is 85% of mass from orbit.

insights.claim: Saronic's CTO says a Jones Act waiver let more petroleum products move from the Gulf to California in the first 40 days than in all of the prior year, revealing latent shipping demand; China holds ~50% of global shipbuilding capacity while US commercial shipbuilding is near zero.
insights.speaker: Vib (Saronic CTO)
insights.so_what: US shipbuilding capacity gap is a structural opportunity for new yards like Saronic's Port Alpha.
insights.quote: we moved more petroleum products in the first 40 days than we did all of last year

insights.claim: Saronic has deployed hundreds of Corsairs, rolled Marauder 2 off the line, won a Marine Corps contract for a new ~70-foot ALPV boat, and opened a Brownsville shipyard (Port Alpha); reliability over 5-55 day unmanned missions under 10-20g slamming loads is the core challenge.
insights.speaker: Vib (Saronic CTO)
insights.so_what: Autonomous naval vessels are entering production; reliability/TCO is the moat.

insights.claim: Saronic's CTO argues AI weather models (open-sourced by Nvidia and Google) should be pushed toward 30-day forecasts, with ocean data being the missing input, noting hedge funds would value it.
insights.speaker: Vib (Saronic CTO)
insights.so_what: Long-range weather prediction is an under-invested AI application with commodity-trading value.

insights.claim: Brian Armstrong predicts more human-enhancement drugs will reach trillion-dollar market caps, citing GLP-1s that took Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk to ~$1T of market cap as use shifted from disease to healthy enhancement; he co-founded longevity biotech NewLimit.
insights.speaker: Brian Armstrong (Coinbase CEO)
insights.so_what: Enhancement/longevity biotech as the next mega-cap category.
insights.quote: I think we're going to see other trillion dollar drugs uh come out

insights.claim: Eight Sleep has crossed $1B in cumulative sales, sells in 37 countries (40 by end of Q1) fully direct-to-consumer, reports record-low returns and retention better than Oura, and claims 3-5x higher revenue per employee than other hardware companies.
insights.speaker: Matteo (Eight Sleep CEO)
insights.so_what: Scaled DTC hardware with strong retention; hotel and airline channels are next.
insights.quote: we are crossing a billion dollar in u cumulative sales

insights.claim: Eight Sleep plans to enter five-star hotels soon, modeled on Starlink's airline strategy, is talking to airplane manufacturers, and sees wellness as an exploding tailwind across hospitality and residences.
insights.speaker: Matteo (Eight Sleep CEO)
insights.so_what: New B2B channels could extend the brand beyond DTC.

insights.claim: Andrew Feldman says Cerebras' IPO created more than a thousand millionaires and advises employees not to hold 99% of wealth in one stock, to sell a little via secondary programs, and to park windfalls in money markets rather than rush decisions.
insights.speaker: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras CEO)
insights.so_what: Post-IPO employee selling is rational diversification, not a negative signal.
insights.quote: there's no reason for you to have 99% of your wealth in one stock
